subject.title: [Feature]: When building a work system with OpenClaw as the core, WebUI should remain accessible after the Gateway crashes.

question: Should OpenClaw core own a crash-survivor Control UI static fallback on the Gateway port, or should this remain an operator-supervisor/reverse-proxy responsibility?
rationale: Current code can only serve Control UI while the Gateway process is alive, and adding a same-port fallback changes availability architecture plus security/auth semantics that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design core rescue sidecar
options.body: Core would define a supervised rescue/static sidecar or service handoff with explicit auth, origin, TLS, port ownership, config schema, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document supervisor pattern
options.body: Core would keep the Gateway lean and document systemd, launchd, container, or reverse-proxy supervision as the supported crash-recovery path.

options.title: Defer request
options.body: Leave the feature open without implementation until enterprise deployment demand or a concrete proposal justifies the core surface.

recommendation.title: Design core rescue sidecar
recommendation.body: Core would define a supervised rescue/static sidecar or service handoff with explicit auth, origin, TLS, port ownership, config schema, docs, and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for both browser Control UI and Gateway server boundaries points to steipete.
